home.title: Learn, review and organise,
home.lead: Browse the sign-language alphabet, read the notes from your lectures, and keep your own study notes. It uses the same account as EchoSign.
home.f1b: All 26 fingerspelling letters, each with its own page, prepared at build time so it loads instantly.
home.f2b: Your joined classes with notes, key terms and quizzes, rendered on the server for your account.
home.f3b: Create, edit, pin and search your own notes. Saved in a database and updated instantly on screen.
home.stepsTitle: Three steps from sign-in to study
steps: Use your EchoSign account, or create one in a minute.
Read the notes, key terms and quizzes from the classes you joined.
Write, pin and search study notes saved to your account.
home.ctaBody: Create a free account or sign in with the one you already use on EchoSign.
home.sample: Illustration with sample text, not real classroom data.

signs.title: Sign dictionary
signs.subtitle: ASL fingerspelling A to Z. Pick a letter to see how to make it.
signs.note: Recognition in EchoSign is rule-based and can be wrong. Letters shown as often confused look alike.

languages.title: Languages in EchoSign
languages.subtitle: The caption languages the platform supports right now, from the EchoSign server.
languages.refreshed: This list refreshes about once an hour.
languages.fallback: Showing the built-in list because the server could not be reached.

rendering.title: Rendering lab
rendering.subtitle: The same time stamp, produced four different ways. Reload each page and watch what changes.
rendering.ssgBody: Built once when the site is built. The time never changes until the next build.
rendering.isrBody: Built once, then rebuilt in the background at most once a minute.
rendering.ssrBody: Built on the server for every single request. The time is always now.
rendering.csrBody: The page loads empty, then the browser asks an API for the time.
rendering.chooseBody: Use static for pages that rarely change, incremental for content that changes every so often, server-side for personal or always-fresh pages, and client-side for small interactive parts.
